discovery: Microscopic statistical derivation of black hole entropy from string theory, leading to the gauge/gravity (holographic) correspondence

nominees.name: Juan Maldacena
nominees.affiliation: Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton, USA

motivation: In 1996 Strominger and Vafa counted the bound states of D-branes making up a supersymmetric black hole and reproduced exactly the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, area/4G. This was the first statistical-mechanical derivation of black hole thermodynamics from a quantum theory of gravity and showed that black hole entropy counts real microstates. Maldacena, through his work on black hole microstates and near-horizon limits, turned this programme into the AdS/CFT correspondence (1997): quantum gravity in anti-de Sitter space is exactly equivalent to an ordinary gauge theory. Together these results settled that black hole evolution can be unitary and gave physics a non-perturbative definition of quantum gravity. They have since become an everyday tool for strongly coupled systems, from quark-gluon plasma to condensed matter, and quantum information. Exact tests, such as superconformal indices that reproduce the entropy of AdS black holes, have confirmed the framework with great precision.
